record.original_question: Several known microgeometries maximize absorption for isotropic two-phase composites, including coated-disk and coated-sphere assemblages and certain multiple-rank laminates. Can any of these maximum-absorption geometries be replaced by simpler geometries, ideally periodic ones with only one inclusion per unit cell, while preserving the same optimal absorption behavior?

evidence.quote: Problem 7: Can any of these discovered geometries, having maximum absorption, can be replaced by simpler ones?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider isotropic two-phase composite materials in $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d=2$ or $3$) made from two prescribed lossy materials with given (complex) permittivities (or, more generally, complex moduli with positive imaginary part modeling absorption). For a given volume fraction of the two phases, one seeks microgeometries that maximize the time-averaged absorption (dissipation) under a prescribed macroscopic field, among all isotropic mixtures with the given volume fractions.

Several microgeometries are known to attain the maximum absorption among isotropic two-phase composites: (i) the Hashin coated-disk assemblage in two dimensions and the Hashin coated-sphere assemblage in three dimensions, in which space is filled by similar coated disks/spheres of all sizes with one phase as a core and the other as a concentric coating in a fixed volume ratio; and (ii) certain finite-rank sequential laminates (multiple-rank laminates) constructed by iteratively laminating the two phases in chosen directions and proportions.

Question: Can any of these maximum-absorption geometries be replaced by a simpler microgeometry — ideally a periodic composite with only a single inclusion per unit cell — that achieves exactly the same optimal absorption for the same volume fractions and constituent materials?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any work establishing that the known maximum-absorption microgeometries (Hashin coated-disk/sphere assemblages and multi-rank laminates) can or cannot be replaced by a simpler periodic composite with a single inclusion per unit cell achieving the same optimal absorption. Available results concern Hashin–Shtrikman bounds and effective conductivity/elasticity rather than this replacement question, so the status appears unresolved based on the search.

status_evidence.title: Assemblages of spheres, ellipsoids, and other neutral inclusions — The Theory of Composites
status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference describing coated-sphere assemblages attaining Hashin–Shtrikman bounds; does not address replacement by single-inclusion periodic geometries for maximum absorption.
status_evidence.claim: Background on optimal microgeometries; no replacement result found.

status_evidence.title: Hashin-Shtrikman assemblage of inhomogeneous spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses generalized coated-sphere assemblages attaining bounds; does not provide a simpler periodic single-inclusion equivalent for maximum absorption.
status_evidence.claim: No evidence of resolution of the replacement question.
